name: Global Privacy Control (GPC)
plain: A browser setting that tells every site the person opts out of sale and sharing.
meaning: Sent as Sec-GPC: 1 and navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Legally binding opt out in California, Colorado (Jul 2024), Connecticut and Texas (2025). California fined Sephora $1.2M in 2022 and Healthline $1.55M in 2025 for ignoring it.

access.persistence: Sent on every request while the setting is on
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can tell every site that you opt out of sale and sharing of your data
limits.user_action: You turn on Global Privacy Control in your browser or a privacy extension
can: Send a signal to each site you visit
Tell sites to treat you as opted out of sale and sharing
Apply to every site without clicking a banner on each one
cannot: Force a site to obey, though some laws such as California's require it
Work in Chrome or Safari without an extension
limits.differs: Firefox and Brave have it built in. Chrome, Safari and iPhone browsers need an extension.

story.what_it_is: A browser switch that tells every site you want to opt out of data sale and sharing.

marketing.name: Global Privacy Control
marketing.pitch: The standard describes a signal that lets people tell sites to stop selling or sharing their data, in one setting.

story.for_you: You turn it on once in your browser or an add on. Then you do not have to click opt out on each site. You will not see it work, but you may see fewer personal ads.
story.for_makers: In several US states, honoring GPC is the law, and fines have hit sites that ignore it. Makers must read the signal and turn off sale and sharing tags. Doing it well also builds trust.

use_cases.example: A retailer reads the GPC signal and stops sending your visit to ad networks that would use it for targeting.
A tag manager rule turns off ad tags for visitors who send GPC, while basic counting stays on.
A news site shows no personalized ads to you when GPC is on.
A game portal reads GPC and does not share a player's data with ad partners.
A privacy team tests every year that GPC visitors do not trigger ad tags, to avoid fines.
A regulator tests sites with a browser that sends GPC, and checks the cookies that appear.

risks: Only works if the site honors it
Not on by default in all browsers

technical_bounds: Default on in Brave and DuckDuckGo
No native Chrome or Safari setting found
A site may ignore it where no law applies

abuse: Not applicable, but a fingerprinting bit
